Steroids flood the brain, **binding to glucocorticoid receptors on dopaminergic neurons** in the limbic system. That directly **upregulates dopamine synthesis and release** — no immune surprise needed. The cat's out because **excess dopamine in the mesolimbic pathway** drives positive psychotic symptoms like hallucinations and delusions. **This isn't an autoimmune encephalitis** — no antibodies, no CSF pleocytosis. You're close. Cortisol doesn't sit in the synthetic pathway — it sits **upstream as a regulator**. Glucocorticoid receptors on dopamine neurons act as **transcription factors**. When steroid binds, it **enters the nucleus and alters gene expression** — specifically, it **increases transcription of tyrosine hydroxylase**, the rate-limiting enzyme that converts tyrosine to L-DOPA. More enzyme means **more dopamine synthesis per neuron per second**. So cortisol isn't a substrate — it's a **gas pedal on the factory floor**. At the bedside, that means **steroid dose and duration correlate directly with psychosis risk**.
